lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2022, BMW started offering British drivers heated front seats. For fifteen pounds a month.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The heaters were already inside the seats. Fitted at the factory. Customers weren't paying for heat. They were paying for permission.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: It's right there. It's like sitting on a radiator that isn't speaking to me.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2023, BMW dropped the idea. Not many people signed up.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Not many.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I'm still paying for Weekend Plus.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He hasn't had a weekend since he signed up. He works Saturdays now. To pay for Weekend Plus.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So. Why is everything a subscription now?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Subscriptions used to be for things that actually run out. Milk. Newspapers.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then, in 2013, Adobe announced that new versions of Photoshop would only come by subscription.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I had one of those. You put it on a shelf, and it was just yours.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then cars. Printers. Toothbrushes.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And companies worked out that their most valuable customer isn't the one who loves the product. It's the one who's forgotten about it.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: To be fair, some of it is brilliant. Nearly any song you can think of, on a bus, for a monthly fee. Teenage me would have wept.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I also pay for a meditation app. I've opened it twice. Every morning it sends me a notification reminding me to breathe.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I still breathe. But now it's out of spite.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2022, the research firm C plus R gave a thousand Americans ten seconds to guess what they spent on subscriptions each month.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The average guess was eighty-six dollars.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then they listed every subscription, one by one.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The average came to two hundred and nineteen.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And forty-two percent admitted they'd stopped using something they were still paying for.

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: Don't open the statement. If you don't look, it's free.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So who is signing us up for all this?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2006, two economists published a study of three American gyms.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Members paying over seventy dollars a month went, on average, four point three times a month.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: That's more than seventeen dollars a visit. A ten-visit pass would have cost them ten.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Their best explanation was overconfidence. People sign up for a much more disciplined version of themselves.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Everyone has one. He's the reason there's a yoga mat behind your door, still in its plastic.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: This is Ryan's. Future Ryan.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He gets up at six, he's read the terms and conditions, and he signed Ryan up for the gym. And the meal kit. And the language app.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: He made a risotto. On a Tuesday. I didn't know you were allowed.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Ryan pays for all of it. Future Ryan uses all of it.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: He speaks Portuguese now. I hear him on the phone, laughing. I don't know what about.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then Future Ryan met someone. At the gym.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Ryan's gym.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Last month, Future Ryan moved to Lisbon.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He left a lovely note. He didn't cancel anything.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: He's taken the air fryer.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So Ryan decided to cancel everything. He started with Weekend Plus, which can only be cancelled in person, on a Saturday.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So he took a Saturday off. Unpaid.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Ryan. Come in. Nobody's in trouble. I've moved to Retention.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I'd like to cancel Weekend Plus, please.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Of course. That's completely valid. Can I ask why?

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I have to work weekends to pay for it.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: So what I'm hearing is, you love it so much, you work for it.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: That's not what he said.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: What if we paused it? You'd keep paying, but the weekends would stop.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: That's what's happening now.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: It's been asking about you.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Is it eating?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: It gets Sunday evenings.

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: Fake your death.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: What if I died?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Then we'd need you to come in. In person.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Of course, if you're sure, cancellations are just through there. Take your time. Most people do.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: That part was made up.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: This part isn't. In 2023, the US Federal Trade Commission sued Amazon over Prime.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It said cancelling took four pages, six clicks and fifteen options, and that inside Amazon this was known as the Iliad Flow.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The Iliad is a poem about a war that lasts ten years. Somebody chose that name. For the way out.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The FTC said Amazon's leaders slowed or rejected changes that would have made cancelling easier, because those changes hurt the bottom line.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In its words, the process existed "not to enable subscribers to cancel, but to stop them."

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2025, Amazon settled for two and a half billion dollars, without admitting wrongdoing.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Adobe was sued too.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The government said that cancelling in your first year could cost half of what you had left to pay, and that the warning was in small print, or behind tiny icons you had to hover over.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In March 2026, Adobe agreed to settle for a hundred and fifty million dollars. Half of it was a fine. The other half was paid in free Adobe.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2024, the FTC adopted a rule that cancelling had to be as easy as signing up.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In July 2025, six days before businesses had to comply, a federal appeals court threw it out. The FTC had skipped a required cost analysis.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The law Amazon settled under still stands. And in March 2026, the FTC started again. From the beginning.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Meanwhile, the newest idea is charging monthly for things you've already bought.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In January 2024, HP's chief executive told CNBC that the company's long-term objective was "to make printing a subscription."

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He also said a customer who doesn't print enough, or doesn't use HP's supplies, is "a bad investment."

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I've never been an investment before. I don't think I'm doing very well.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And if you cancel HP's Instant Ink, the cartridges already in your printer stop working at the end of the billing cycle.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Which is usually when someone online says: you'll own nothing, and be happy.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It isn't a secret plan. It comes from a short World Economic Forum video in 2016, based on an essay by the Danish politician Ida Auken, imagining life in a city in 2030.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: She later wrote that it wasn't her utopia, just a scenario to get people talking.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The internet decided it was a threat.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Brayden decided it was a goal.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Nine days later, Ryan went round with a housewarming present.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Bro! The door's on the premium tier. Window's free. Mind the roses, they're rented.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: I don't own anything anymore. Sofa's on demand. Even my hairline's on a subscription. Ownership is an anchor. I'm a boat.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Fridge light's on pause. Keeps me hungry.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Where do you sit?

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Sitting's on the Plus plan. I stand. Standing's free.

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: Lie down. Make it worth it.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: It's like visiting someone who's been burgled. And they're proud of it.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: And for nine ninety-nine a month, you can subscribe to me. You get my mornings. Most of them are filmed in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: I can't take that. Then I'd own it.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So, why is everything a subscription now? Partly because some things genuinely work better that way. I'm keeping my music.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: But mostly because a subscription is a bet on three things. That you'll forget. That you'll overestimate the person you're about to become. And that leaving will be just annoying enough to put off until next month.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: A decent test is whether you'd sign up again today, at today's price. If you wouldn't, it's not a subscription anymore. It's a monthly charge you keep for sentimental reasons.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Really sorry about this one.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It took him the whole evening.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: This one's mine.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Hi Ryan. It's Gerald. Nobody's in trouble. We noticed you'd left, so we've signed you up for Weekend Lite. The first month's completely free.
